chains.title: AR binds the T allele more at the rs339331 enhancer and regulates RFX6
chains.cell_type: prostate cancer cells/tumors; LNCaP clone FGC (ACH-000977) is the supplied expression context

links.claim: AR binds the ref T allele more strongly than the alt C allele at rs339331 in prostate cancer chromatin; E06c reports that the T allele enhances AR chromatin occupancy. AR is not named in the supplied QBiC-SELEX screen rows, so its QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked; no AR own-model or mapped row is provided, and no other TF's binding change is used as AR evidence.
rs339331 lies within cCRE EH38E2496909, a distal enhancer-like element, making it a plausible allele-specific regulatory element.

RFX6 is the nearest protein-coding gene and the strongest L2G gene in credible sets containing this variant; E06d reports an enhancer complex at rs339331 increasing RFX6. However, E20 found no significant GTEx v8 prostate eQTL for this variant, so a direct prostate eQTL link is not supported by that dataset.

The relevant cell type is prostate cancer, with LNCaP (ACH-000977) as the supplied expression context and AR occupancy at this element described in prostate cancer tumors. E18 reports no ENCODE AR ChIP-seq peak containing rs339331 in LNCaP, with the caveat that absence can also mean no AR experiment in that biosample, so LNCaP-specific AR occupancy is not established by the supplied ChIP data.

rs339331 is associated with prostate cancer risk at 6q22, and the locus has been repeatedly associated with prostate cancer across populations. The allelic direction is conflicting: E04 reports C as the strongest prostate-cancer effect allele, whereas E06c calls T the risk allele.

predictions: The T allele should show higher AR occupancy at the rs339331 enhancer than C.
If AR activates RFX6, T should increase RFX6; if AR represses RFX6, C with lower AR occupancy could increase RFX6 and fit the C effect allele reported in E04.
The chain predicts an AR-dependent, allele-specific enhancer effect at rs339331 in prostate cancer cells.
falsified_if: Allele-specific AR ChIP at rs339331 does not show higher AR occupancy on the T allele.
AR perturbation does not change RFX6 expression or enhancer activity in an rs339331-dependent manner.
The T-allele AR-occupancy report is not reproducible, or the C allele is shown to increase AR occupancy instead.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs339331
predictions: No TF-mediated allelic effect of rs339331 on RFX6 or any other nearby gene.
The prostate cancer association is explained by a linked causal variant in the 6q22 credible set, by LD with another regulatory variant, or by a non-allelic mechanism.
E20 found no significant GTEx v8 prostate eQTL for rs339331, which is consistent with the null but does not prove it.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TF binding and reporter assays show a reproducible, RFX6-dependent effect of rs339331 itself rather than a linked variant.
Fine-mapping resolves the causal variant to rs339331 with a direct allelic regulatory effect.

chains.title: HOXB13 binds the T allele more at the rs339331 enhancer and may modulate RFX6
chains.cell_type: prostate cancer cells/tumors; LNCaP clone FGC (ACH-000977) expression context

links.claim: HOXB13 has an own QBiC-SELEX model in group G024; the best HOXB13 model scores z -103.49 with effect -4.771, meaning the alt C allele binds HOXB13 less and the ref T allele binds more. Within G024, HOXB13 is selected over related homeodomain TFs because it has the strongest own-model score and is highly expressed in the LNCaP context at 182.31 TPM; E06d also implicates HOXB13 at this enhancer. This is an in vitro binding prediction, not allele-specific ChIP evidence.
rs339331 lies in dELS EH38E2496909, and HOXB13 has been reported in a GATA2/SMAD4/HOXB13 transcriptional complex at the rs339331/6q22 enhancer.

RFX6 is the nearest gene and best L2G target of the credible sets containing this variant; E06d reports that the HOXB13-containing complex at this enhancer increases RFX6 expression. E20 found no significant GTEx v8 prostate eQTL for this variant, so direct prostate eQTL support is absent.

HOXB13 is expressed in the prostate cancer LNCaP expression context at 182.31 TPM. E19 reports no ENCODE HOXB13 ChIP-seq peak containing rs339331 in LNCaP, with the caveat that absence can also mean no HOXB13 experiment in that biosample, so LNCaP-specific HOXB13 occupancy is not established.

rs339331 at the RFX6/6q22 locus is associated with prostate cancer risk. The direction is problematic: if T binds HOXB13 more and the HOXB13 complex increases RFX6, T would be expected to be risk, but E04 reports C as the strongest prostate-cancer effect allele.

predictions: The T allele should have more HOXB13 occupancy than C at this enhancer.
If HOXB13 is activating, T should increase RFX6; if HOXB13 is repressive in this context, C with less HOXB13 could increase RFX6 and fit the C effect allele from E04.
This chain distinguishes itself from the AR chain by depending on HOXB13, not AR, for the allele-specific occupancy.
falsified_if: Allele-specific HOXB13 ChIP at rs339331 does not show T > C binding.
HOXB13 loss-of-function does not change RFX6 expression or enhancer activity from this element.
The HOXB13-containing complex is shown not to act at this enhancer or not to affect RFX6.

chains.title: IRF6 binds the C allele more at the rs339331 enhancer and may regulate RFX6
chains.cell_type: prostate cancer LNCaP clone FGC (ACH-000977) expression context

links.claim: IRF6 has an own QBiC-SELEX model in group G080; the best IRF6 model scores z 56.39 with effect 2.918, meaning the alt C allele binds IRF6 more strongly. Within G080, IRF6 is selected over IRF5 because IRF6 has the stronger own-model score and higher expression in the LNCaP context at 38.37 TPM versus IRF5 at 5.53 TPM. This is an in vitro binding prediction only.

rs339331 lies within the distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, so an allele-specific IRF6 site could act through this element. No IRF6 occupancy or allele-specific activity at this element is shown.

RFX6 is the nearest gene and the strongest L2G target in credible sets containing rs339331; however, direct IRF6-to-RFX6 regulatory evidence is not provided, and E20 found no significant GTEx v8 prostate eQTL for this variant.
IRF6 is expressed in the supplied prostate cancer LNCaP expression context at 38.37 TPM, making it a candidate TF in this cell type.
rs339331 is associated with prostate cancer risk, and E04 reports C as the strongest prostate-cancer effect allele, which matches the IRF6 alt-C binding direction if IRF6 is activating.

predictions: The C allele should increase IRF6 occupancy at the rs339331 enhancer.
If IRF6 activates RFX6, C should increase RFX6 expression and provide a straightforward C-risk-allele mechanism.
If IRF6 represses RFX6, the predicted direction of RFX6 expression would reverse.
falsified_if: Allele-specific IRF6 ChIP at rs339331 does not show C > T binding.
IRF6 perturbation does not change RFX6 expression or enhancer activity in prostate cancer cells.
IRF6 is not expressed or not active in the relevant prostate cancer cell type.

Dysregulated expression or mutations of the RFX6 gene in prostate cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, melanoma, and other tumors have garnered significant interest, with studies showing that such alterations affect tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and are correlated with an unfavorable clinical prognosis in patients carrying RFX6 mutations.

Here the FinnGen cohort phenome-wide analysis, along with multiple genome-wide association studies, has consistently identified the rs339331-RFX6/6q22 locus associated with prostate cancer (PCa) risk across diverse populations.
It is uncovered that rs339331 resides in a reprogrammed androgen receptor (AR) binding site in PCa tumors, with the T risk allele enhancing AR chromatin occupancy.

Strinkingly, GATA2 and SMAD4 globally mediated inherited PCa risk and formed a transcriptional complex with HOXB13 at the PCa risk-associated rs339331/6q22 enhancer, leading to increased expression of the PCa susceptibility gene RFX6.
Notable genes of interest include HCP5, RFX6 and H3C1 for risk, and MKI67 and KLF5 for aggressive disease.
